title: Data Is Sometimes the Best Answer for Overcoming Resistance to Feedback
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article addresses team members who repeatedly reject feedback about their own behavior, arguing that when persuasion fails, aggregated data from multiple sources can succeed where individual conversations can't. The author's memorable framing is that when a dozen people independently describe the same pattern, it becomes very hard to dismiss as one person's opinion. The recommended approach is to deliberately over-collect data and present it in a structured, unemotional way so the case becomes effectively unassailable. The piece notes an ironic twist: resistant team members often expect the data collection to vindicate their own self-view, only to be confronted with the opposite.
points: Some team members persistently resist feedback about their own behavior no matter how it's delivered individually.
Aggregated data from multiple credible sources can break through resistance that direct conversation cannot.
The recommended approach is to intentionally over-collect data and present it in a structured, unemotional format.
Resistant team members often expect the data-gathering process to vindicate their self-view, which makes the eventual reveal more powerful.
quotes: Data, when collected and presented well, is undeniable. It sets the record straight like nothing else can.
Think of it this way. When 12 people who know you well tell you that you walk and quack like a duck, you do.
To ensure the point is made, they will typically collect more data than they even need to.
Many will expect the data to confirm their views, not negate them.
Perception is a reality impossible to deny if it comes from many places.
